title: App Service Deployment Slots
description: Use deployment slots to test changes safely and swap them into production with zero downtime.

data.text: Deployment slots are separate instances of your app that share the same App Service plan. You can deploy to a staging slot, test it, and then swap it with production. The swap is almost instant and keeps your production app running.
A slot has its own hostname, content, and configuration. Common slots are staging, testing, or canary. They live inside the same App Service plan, so there is no extra compute cost for having them.

data.title: Benefits of Slots
items: Test a new release in production settings before going live
Warm up the app before swapping to avoid cold starts
Swap content and configuration in one operation
Rollback instantly by swapping back to the previous slot

data.text: Swapping exchanges the content and settings between two slots. You can also swap with a preview to see what will happen before the swap completes.

data.title: Azure CLI — Swap Slots
data.content: Swap the staging slot into production
data.code:
# Swap the staging slot into production
az webapp deployment slot swap \
  --resource-group MyResourceGroup \
  --name MyWebApp \
  --slot staging \
  --target-slot production

# Preview a swap without completing it
az webapp deployment slot swap \
  --resource-group MyResourceGroup \
  --name MyWebApp \
  --slot staging \
  --target-slot production \
  --action preview

data.text: Not every setting should swap. Slot-specific settings, such as production database connection strings, stay with the slot. This prevents staging from overwriting production secrets.

data.title: Typical Slot Settings
items: Third-party API keys used by production
CORS origins that should remain different between environments
Any setting that must not change during a swap

data.title: Testing in Production
data.text: After swapping, the old production code moves to the staging slot. If you notice a problem, swap back immediately. Both slots remain available for quick rollbacks.

terms.definition: A live app instance hosted inside an App Service plan, used for staging or testing before production.
The process of exchanging the content and configuration of two slots, usually staging and production.
A configuration value that stays with a specific slot and does not move during a swap.
A dry-run swap that shows what would change without actually modifying the slots.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Deployment slots let you test changes before releasing to production.
Swapping is fast and keeps the app online.
Use slot-specific settings to protect production secrets during swaps.
Always have a rollback plan: if the new version fails, swap back immediately.
data.takeaway: Slots make releases safer and faster by separating testing from production.
